doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

chapter: Early New Orleans experiences and sideman roles
title: Erroll Garner's quartet at the Stage Door Canteen
summary: As a high school senior he led the house trio with Walter Lastie and received piano lessons from Garner during a two-week booking.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Wow. You hung out with Danny Barker and Erroll Garner?

Well in my senior year of high school I had a gig with Walter Lastie, it was my gig but Walter Lastie was the drummer. He was one of Herlin Riley’s uncles, and we had a band when Herlin Riley played trumpet. He played trumpet before he played drums. And a bass player, and Sam Alcorn, a great trumpet player, and we had a gig at the top of a hotel, it was late night, I missed all my morning classes. And then we transitioned to a club on Bourbon Street, a mob joint called the Stage Door Canteen, which was modeled, actually the same people as the one in New York. And we were the house trio. We played behind — they’d bring in comics, we played behind them. We’d play our own set. And for two weeks they brought in the Erroll Garner Quartet. Erroll Garner. Jimmy Smith on — the drummer Jimmy Smith. Eugene Wright –- McCarney I think it was, on bass, and Jose Manuala on trumpet. It was so killing. And during those two weeks Erroll Garner gave me some piano lessons. So that’s how I got to hang out with him. Yeah.
